aspects.says: A String stores its characters in Latin-1 at one byte each when all of them are at most U+00FF, and otherwise in UTF-16 at two bytes each, for the whole string.
basis: section:A String Keeps Latin-1 Text at One Byte per Character, and One Character Beyond Latin-1 Doubles It

aspects.says: A String built from an array copies it, and toCharArray returns a copy, so later changes to the array never reach the String.
basis: section:A String Copies What It Is Built From, So Nothing Changes It Afterwards

aspects.says: Bytes become text only through a charset; new String(bytes) uses the default, UTF-8 since Java 18, so data in another charset must have its charset named.
basis: section:Bytes Become Text Only Through a Charset, and new String(bytes) Picks One for You

aspects.says: Since Java 18 the default charset is UTF-8 whatever the operating system's locale.
basis: section:Bytes Become Text Only Through a Charset, and new String(bytes) Picks One for You

aspects.says: Because a String never changes it caches its hash code, and a secret held in one can't be wiped, which is why passwords are read into a char[].
basis: section:A String Copies What It Is Built From, So Nothing Changes It Afterwards
section:Design Note: Why a String Can Never Change
aspects.reason: neither a cached hash nor a secret left in the heap shows in a graded test's result: one is timing, the other needs a heap dump

aspects.says: intern() returns the pooled string with the same characters and can't change the string it is called on, so only code that stores the returned reference shares one copy.
basis: section:Equal Strings Built at Run Time Are Separate Objects; intern() Shares One Only with Code That Keeps Its Result

aspects.says: new String(bytes, charset) silently replaces undecodable bytes with U+FFFD; a CharsetDecoder set to REPORT, or Files.readString, throws instead.
basis: section:Bytes Become Text Only Through a Charset, and new String(bytes) Picks One for You

aspects.says: Sharing equal strings pays only for fields with few distinct values; interning unique values adds a table entry each and saves nothing.
basis: section:Equal Strings Built at Run Time Are Separate Objects; intern() Shares One Only with Code That Keeps Its Result
